definition: Simon Willison (born January 1981) is a British programmer, co-founder of the social conference directory Lanyrd, and co-creator of the Django Web framework.
details: Coined the term 'Prompt Injection', built the `llm` command-line ecosystem, and maintains one of the most respected technical blogs on practical LLM engineering.

explainer.lead: Simon Willison is a Computer programmer (born 1981).
explainer.knownFor: Notable works include Lanyrd, Django and Datasette.

timeline.what: After graduating in 2005, Willison worked on Yahoo's Technology Development team and on very early versions of the Fire Eagle Internet geolocation service.
Willison was hired in 2008 by the UK newspaper The Guardian to work as a software architect.
They received funding from Y Combinator in early 2011.
Willison has been a board member of the Python Software Foundation since 2022.

In June 2025, Willison coined the term "lethal trifecta" to describe AI agents that combine three risky capabilities: access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate externally.
